General Domain Definition: A men's hair system (non-surgical hair replacement system) is an engineered cranial prosthesis consisting of human hair hand-tied or injected into an ultra-thin skin polyurethane membrane (0.03mm–0.08mm) or delicate lace base (Swiss lace, French lace, mono-mesh). It is designed to integrate seamlessly into a man's existing biological hair at the parietal ridge and temples. It must NEVER look like a thick wig, helmet, or synthetic toupee.
Hairline Graduation & Realism: The front hairline is the single most critical quality determinant. In 'hairline:undetectable' presentation, density at the leading 0.5cm must be graduated (starting at 60–70% density with fine baby hairs and single bleached knots), transitioning smoothly into full crown density. There must be ZERO visible lace mesh grid, ZERO blunt or thickened polyurethane edges, and NO perfectly straight ruler-like hair lines.
Hair Color & Grey Percentage Rubric: Hair colors must follow international hair system standards: #1 (Jet Black), #1B (Natural / Off Black), #2 (Darkest Brown), #3 (Dark Brown), #4 (Medium Brown), #5 (Medium-Light Brown), #6 (Light Brown), #7 (Ash Brown), and #22 (Light Blonde). Grey hair must be specified as an exact percentage (e.g., #1B20 indicates 20% grey hair blend), naturally concentrated at the temples and sideburns to match biological aging patterns.
Curl & Wave Pattern Accuracy: Hair wave and curl diameter must be mechanically accurate: Straight (32mm rod), Slight Wave (25mm rod - natural relaxed men's hair), Body Wave (20mm rod - light bounce and movement), Medium Wave (15mm rod), Tight Wave (10mm rod), or Afro Curl (4mm–8mm). The curl pattern of the hair system MUST match the curl pattern of the subject's remaining biological hair at the temples and back.
Before-and-After Transformation Rules: Before-and-after comparisons must show an authentic, grounded transformation: The 'Before' state accurately portrays male pattern baldness (Norwood Scale 3 to 6) with scalp skin pores, thinning frontal vertex, and intact biological hair on sides and back. The 'After' state shows the same individual with an impeccably blended hair system matching their natural color, age-appropriate density, and temple blend. Face identity, lighting, camera angle, and background must remain consistent across both states.
Base Material Taxonomy: The base construction must match the designated type: 'base:poly-skin' (translucent micro-thin polyurethane matching scalp skin tone, hair appears growing directly from scalp), 'base:swiss-lace' (maximum breathability, undetectable edge, soft bleached knots), 'base:french-lace' (durable, fine mesh for active lifestyles), or 'base:mono-mesh' (honeycomb monofilament for high durability with polyurethane perimeter).
Aesthetic & Brand Tone (Atelier Zero v7): All media must reflect editorial realism, quiet luxury, and craftsmanship. Color palette: Ink (#0D0D0D), Bone (#F9F8F6), Paper (#F2EFEB), Line (#DDD7CE), and Atelier Coral (#FF6B4A). Grounded physical studio lighting with soft falloff and natural dynamic range. No synthetic AI airbrushing, no waxy plastic skin, and no fake beauty filters.
Brand Prohibitions (Strict Don'ts): Strictly prohibited: 1. Dense, abrupt 'wall of hair' hairlines. 2. Unblended transitions between system hair and biological side hair. 3. Over-saturated artificial hair dye without tonal variation. 4. Visible lace netting or shiny poly glue lines. 5. Altering the subject's facial anatomy or identity between before and after frames. 6. Trademark symbols ('™', '®', '©') or watermarks.
